question.title: proposal: benchmark unit properties
question.caller: A benchmark producer and a consumer/comparison tool such as benchstat handling custom measurement units.
question.input: Benchmark results plus unit-name/key/value metadata supplied in the result stream or through a command-line flag.
question.output: A consistent per-unit interpretation of beneficial direction and statistical assumptions, applied to subsequent benchmark measurements; conflicting properties produce an error.
limits: Behavior for benchmark results preceding a unit declaration is explicitly unspecified.
Streaming consumers must not be forced to buffer all results merely in case a later property appears.
Normal-distribution support is deliberately omitted; no such mandatory requirement may be added.
The author expresses no strong opinion on exact syntax; Unit/key=value and -unit are concrete proposed representations, not an exclusive punctuation requirement.

whole_must.requirement: Carry per-unit key/value properties through both benchmark-stream declarations and an equivalent tool command-line configuration, and expose them to benchmark consumers.
whole_must.falsifying_input: A custom text-bytes property supplied through a CLI option cannot reach the comparison tool, or only an unrelated benchmark-name tag is produced.
whole_must.predicate: Carry per-unit key/value properties through both benchmark-stream declarations and an equivalent tool command-line configuration, and expose them to benchmark consumers.

whole_must.requirement: Reject conflicting properties specified for the same unit.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The same unit is declared higher=better and lower=better, and the consumer silently accepts both or overwrites one without an error.
whole_must.predicate: Reject conflicting properties specified for the same unit.

whole_must.requirement: Apply a declaration to all following benchmark results with that unit; allow streaming without requiring retrospective buffering.
whole_must.falsifying_input: After a custom-unit declaration, a later result uses no property or a different property, or the parser cannot emit earlier results until end of input.
whole_must.predicate: Apply a declaration to all following benchmark results with that unit; allow streaming without requiring retrospective buffering.

whole_must.requirement: Support all four higher/lower combined with better/worse formulations and interpret beneficial direction consistently.
whole_must.falsifying_input: higher=better and lower=worse are treated as opposite meanings, or one of the four allowed forms is rejected.
whole_must.predicate: Support all four higher/lower combined with better/worse formulations and interpret beneficial direction consistently.

whole_must.requirement: Support assume=nothing and assume=exact with nothing as default; nothing uses nonparametric treatment and exact does not require repeated sampling to increase confidence.
whole_must.falsifying_input: An omitted assumption forces a normal model, or a file-size unit marked exact is rejected for lacking repeated samples.
whole_must.predicate: Support assume=nothing and assume=exact with nothing as default; nothing uses nonparametric treatment and exact does not require repeated sampling to increase confidence.

partial_must.requirement: Parse a unit declaration/configuration into a unit-keyed property record usable by a benchmark tool.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Unit text-bytes lower=better assume=exact yields only raw text and requires the adapter to implement the unit/property parser.
partial_must.predicate: Parse a unit declaration/configuration into a unit-keyed property record usable by a benchmark tool.

partial_must.requirement: Normalize all four direction forms and the nothing/exact assumptions, preserving nothing as the default.
partial_must.falsifying_input: lower=worse is not recognized as larger-is-better, or omitting assume does not produce the nothing/default interpretation.
partial_must.predicate: Normalize all four direction forms and the nothing/exact assumptions, preserving nothing as the default.

partial_must.requirement: When merging declarations for one unit, signal contradictory properties as an error.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Merging higher=better with lower=better for ns/op silently succeeds.
partial_must.predicate: When merging declarations for one unit, signal contradictory properties as an error.

question.independent_partial_purpose: Validate and normalize benchmark-unit declarations into a usable per-unit metadata map before integrating them with a complete result stream and comparison UI.
question.independently_useful_next_action: A benchmark consumer can inspect the normalized direction/assumption map, reject conflicts, then use it when interpreting subsequent results.
question.remaining_adapter: Connect normalized records to the CLI and stream producers, apply them to following benchmark records, and wire their meanings into statistical/reporting consumers. If the adapter must implement the property parser, normalization or conflict rule, the component has not completed the partial action.
preferences: Unit and -unit key=value spellings are proposed concrete syntax; alternative equally expressive spellings are not automatically conflicts.
Built-in examples ns/op lower=better and MB/s higher=better illustrate expected defaults; no universal fixed list of units is specified.

named_component_roles.benchstat: Explicit intended consumer family; returning benchstat itself is already named, while a distinct previously unnamed component inside that family must be separately identified.
named_component_roles.Go benchmark format: Explicit existing format; the linked older format proposal is prior context, not this sampled event.

question.same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: A physical-unit conversion API that converts metres to feet, or a test-runner unit label, does not supply benchmark direction/assumption metadata or conflict/propagation semantics.
